primitives.verbatim_quote: Via the Rao-Blackwell theorem, we propose a shot-make probability model that conditions probability estimates on shot trajectory information, thereby reducing the variance of the new estimator relative to standard FG%.

primitives.breakdown_regime: When shot trajectory data is unavailable or noisy, RB-FG% reverts to standard FG%.

primitives.verbatim_quote: Next we use these factors to model shot-make probabilities for all shots in the 2014-15 season, and use these probabilities to produce a Rao-Blackwellized FG% estimator (RB-FG%) for each player.

primitives.name: Trajectory Feature Extraction
primitives.verbatim_quote: We obtain shooting information by using optical tracking data to estimate three factors for each shot: entry angle, shot depth, and left-right accuracy.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\alpha_i': 'entry angle of shot i (degrees)', 'd_i': 'shot depth of shot i (feet)', 'a_i': 'left-right accuracy of shot i (feet)'}
primitives.assumptions: Optical tracking data provides accurate spatial coordinates; trajectory can be approximated by quadratic model.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Tracking data loss or sensor error leads to imprecise feature estimation.

layer2.mapping: Extracted features form the input kernel for the shot-make model in GSE's predictive pipeline.
layer2.telemetry: Precision of estimated shot features compared to ground truth.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in applying the Rao-Blackwell theorem to field goal percentage estimation. Standard FG% suffers from high variance due to small sample sizes and noise in shot outcomes. By conditioning on shot trajectory features—entry angle, depth, and accuracy—the proposed RB-FG% estimator reduces variance while preserving unbiasedness. The derivation begins with defining the sufficient statistic (shot trajectory features) and applying the theorem to yield a lower-variance estimator. This approach leverages the structure of shot data to improve inference, particularly for rare events like 3-pointers. The shot-make probability model is then constructed using logistic regression, conditioned on these features. The resulting RB-FG% becomes a more stable proxy for shooting skill, especially early in seasons or for players with limited shot samples. The failure mode occurs when trajectory data is absent or inaccurate, reverting to standard FG%.
